rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 8 (score 654.0, best so far) had kp 5.0, kd 1.2, body 0.10 x 0.08, base 1.1, and 5 sensors at x = -0.07 to 0.07. It finished 18/20 on the oval, 19/20 on the s-bend, and 0/20 on the slalom, where progress was 0.47 and every run went off track at the 0.06 m limit. Iteration 9 raised kp to 5.4 and kd to 1.4. The slalom barely moved (progress 0.476), while s-bend finishes fell from 19 to 15 and the score dropped to 638. So extra steering gain is not the slalom limit, and it costs s-bend performance. Line loss is rare (0.65 events per slalom run), so the robot is drifting off the tape on alternating curves rather than losing it. The slalom is the bottleneck for the score.

Changes. (1) Revert the controller to the iteration 8 gains (kp 5.0, kd 1.2), which gave the best s-bend result. (2) Move from 5 to 7 sensors on the same span (x = -0.07 to 0.07, y = 0.08). Spacing drops from 0.035 m to about 0.023 m, so the tape is seen with finer lateral resolution near the centre line and the signal changes more smoothly as the line moves across the array. Sensor weights are spaced evenly from -2 to 2, so the signal scale and effective kp match iterations 8 and 9. (3) Geometry otherwise matches iteration 8: body 0.10 x 0.08, mass 0.8, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, sensor_size 0.016, base_speed 1.1, ki 0, last_direction. The off-track limit stays at 0.06 m.

Expected result. The slalom should show progress above 0.5 and possibly a few finishes. The s-bend should stay at or near 19/20 and the oval at 18 to 20/20, with steering_oscillation at or below about 0.18. Score should be at or above iteration 8.

Hypotheses. (H1) Slalom failure comes from coverage and signal resolution on alternating curves, so a denser array will lower its max_error and line_loss_events. (H2) Iteration 9's loss on the s-bend came from the higher kp, so reverting kp restores s-bend finishes. (H3) If the slalom stays at about 0.47 progress, the limit is response speed rather than sensing. The next step would then be a lower base_speed with the same gains, or a shorter body to cut yaw inertia further.

Measurements requested: per-track completion, progress, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort, to separate coverage loss from lag.
